key_insight: MELD-graph detected focal cortical dysplasia at 7T with similar sensitivity to 3T, but specificity was notably worse unless harmonisation was used.
clinical_relevance: For epilepsy imaging workflows, 7T MELD-graph may help flag difficult lesions for review, but its higher false-positive rate means results should be interpreted cautiously.
method: Paired 3T and 7T MRI from 23 FCD patients and 39 healthy controls across four epilepsy centres.
Compared MELD-graph on 3T, on 7T default settings, and on 7T with adaptations for bias correction, skull-stripping, and sub-millimetric reconstruction.
Tested the effect of ComBat harmonisation and assessed surface morphometry plus lesion detection performance.
evidence_signal: In this multi-centre evaluation, sensitivity was 65% at 3T versus 48-52% at 7T, while specificity dropped from 76% at 3T to 39-45% at 7T and improved with ComBat harmonisation.
watch_item: 7T outputs produced more false positives, especially in the basal temporal lobes, so the pipeline should not be used as a stand-alone decision tool.
paper_title: Multi-centre validation of MELD-graph for automated focal cortical dysplasia detection using 7T compared to paired 3T MRI
